clue.text: Several different grades written in teacher's margin notes

indicators.note: the grades are set down inside the word for the teacher, as text is written in a space

parts.note: sir is how a pupil addresses a male teacher
four separate exam grades, D, E, B and A

explanation.surface: A teacher scribbles a range of marks in the margins of pupils' work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Several different grades' is any handful of letter grades; here D, E, B and A go inside SIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidebar is a short boxed or marginal comment set beside the main text, much like notes in a margin.

clue.text: Get the better of naughty rascal at home, leading to end of fun

indicators.note: a naughty child misbehaves, so these letters are disordered
only the last letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A mischievous child at home wrecks the fun in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' scrambles RASCAL AT HOME, and N, the end of 'fun', follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To steal a march on someone is an idiom for gaining an advantage over them by acting first.

clue.text: Mug consumes pot daily

indicators.note: consuming means taking inside, so the face swallows the pot

parts.note: mug and dial are both slang for the face
an urn is a large pot

explanation.surface: A cup holds the teapot's contents every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' looks like a cup, but it is slang for the face, DIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Diurnal means happening every day or by day, so it serves as daily.

clue.text: Sea captain contracted disease

indicators.note: contracted means shortened, so the last letter of the plant disease is cut

parts.note: blight is a plant disease

explanation.surface: A ship's captain caught an illness at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted' reads as caught, but it signals shortening. Bligh was captain of the Bounty, famed for its mutiny.
explanation.definitionFit: William Bligh was the naval captain of HMS Bounty, set adrift by mutineers in 1789.

clue.text: Spread more germs? Following hospital treatment, that's under control

indicators.note: in a down answer, the pieces placed under come after

parts.note: a rein is a means of control
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
ECT, electroconvulsive therapy, is a hospital treatment

explanation.surface: After hospital care, is the patient's infection now contained, or spreading more germs?
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' places F and ECT below REIN in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinfect is to pass an infection on again, a fair question-marked sense of spreading germs anew.

clue.text: Band stuck in hotel lift, in a spin

indicators.note: spinning round means the hidden letters are read backwards
the answer is lodged inside the run of letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A band of musicians is trapped in a hotel lift that is going round and round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck in' hides TELLIF inside 'hotel lift'; 'in a spin' turns it round. 'Band' looks like musicians but means a strip.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillet is a narrow strip or ribbon, such as a headband or a narrow band of wood or moulding.

clue.text: Passionate about new clothes

indicators.note: about means around, so the passionate word goes round the letter for new

parts.note: fiery means passionate or hot-tempered

explanation.surface: Someone is enthusiastic about their new outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Finery means smart or showy clothing, one's best dress.

clue.text: Windows no longer working? Time to switch off

definitions.meaning: windows, as lights or panes letting in light, are out of action
the hour when lamps are turned off, as in a dormitory

explanation.surface: A computer failure is a cue to shut down.
explanation.definitionFit: Lights out is bedtime in a barracks or dormitory, and read literally it says the windows are dark.

clue.text: Passage from old publication

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a tract is a short published pamphlet

explanation.surface: A section taken from a long-gone book or paper.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract is a passage taken from a longer text.

clue.text: I tried desperately to get in university, showing scholarship

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take in, or let in, the university letter
acting desperately suggests wild flailing, so the letters of these words are thrown into disorder

parts.note: a play that is showing is on

explanation.surface: A struggling applicant tried hard to win a university place and proved their learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperately' scrambles I TRIED to ERDITI, and 'to get in' puts U inside it after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholarship here means deep learning, the knowledge gained by study, not a grant of money.

clue.text: Position, say, in reverse gear

indicators.note: running in reverse means these letters are read from the end back to the start

parts.note: to position something is to put it
say introduces an example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: A driver positions the stick, so to speak, in reverse gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in reverse' turns PUTEG into the answer. 'gear' looks like part of a car, but it means clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear is informal for clothes, and a get-up is an outfit or costume, often a striking one.

clue.text: Very unusual bird eaten by creature, except head and tail, in China

indicators.note: the built letters sit inside the word for China

parts.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate) for mate, so a pal

indicators.note: being eaten puts the bird inside the trimmed creature
the first and last letters of the word creature are dropped

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A bird swallowed by a beast in China is a strange affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country but is rhyming slang: china plate = mate, PAL. REATUR (creature, 'except head and tail') eats TERN, and the lot goes 'in' PAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Preternatural means beyond what is normal or natural, so extraordinary.

clue.text: It's clear I would leave around noon, wanting hot meal

indicators.note: the remaining letters go round the letter for noon
the shortened form of the two words departs from the word for clear

parts.note: a clear explanation is lucid
I would contracts to I'd
N is short for noon, as on a clock face
H stands for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: It's obvious I'd be leaving about midday, keen on a hot meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I would' is read as its contraction, so 'leave' takes those two letters out of the word for clear; 'around' then wraps what is left round noon's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunch is the meal eaten at midday, so it is an everyday example of a meal.

clue.text: Splendid maids of honour perhaps retained by queen, even though all wanting retirement

indicators.note: everything built so far needs to retire, that is go backwards
the cakes are held inside the royal letters

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the queen
a maid of honour is a small British custard tart, so these are an example of tarts
if can mean even though, as in 'a pleasant if dull evening'

explanation.surface: Bridesmaids kept on by the queen were excellent, though all of them wanted to retire.
explanation.walkthrough: Maids of honour are small British custard tarts, not bridesmaids. 'all wanting retirement' turns the whole assembled string round, not just one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something of the highest quality, excellent or top-class.

clue.text: Current staff content to be badly run

indicators.note: read as contained, these letters are held inside the staff

parts.note: a mace is a ceremonial staff
ill can mean badly, as in ill-treated
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Employees right now are happy for things to be poorly managed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like happy but is read as contained, and 'staff' is a ceremonial rod rather than employees.
explanation.definitionFit: A millrace is the channel of water whose current drives a mill wheel, so it is a current.

clue.text: Trustworthy person selling posh piece of furniture

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: A dependable salesman offers an upmarket item of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputable means having a good name, so trustworthy.

clue.text: Attack the same point twice that's on the chin

parts.note: to go at someone is to attack them

indicators.note: twice says the same compass letter is used two times over

parts.note: E for east is a compass point

explanation.surface: A boxer is told to strike one spot twice, the spot being the chin.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like boxing advice, but 'point' is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A goatee is a small pointed beard grown on the chin alone.

clue.text: Single cleric absorbed by biblical books? It happens to be of no significance

definitions.text: It happens to be of no significance

indicators.note: absorbed means taken in, so the books surround the other pieces

parts.note: NT is the New Testament
one is a single unit
Ven, for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: An unmarried priest buried in scripture finds it all meaningless.
explanation.walkthrough: VEN is short for Venerable, an archdeacon's title.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-event is an occasion that turns out unimportant or disappointing.

clue.text: One decorating cake perhaps turns page with last of these instructions

indicators.note: turning round means the word for the cake decorator is read backwards

parts.note: someone who covers a cake with icing is an icer

indicators.note: only the final letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A baker icing a cake turns the page to reach the last of the instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' looks like the baker turning the page, but it reverses the cake decorator; 'last of' takes only the final letter of 'these'.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe is a set of directions for making a dish, so it is a set of instructions.

clue.text: Check light in room

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check
amber is a traffic light

explanation.surface: Inspect the lamp in the bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamber is a room, especially a bedroom or private room.

clue.text: Begin to understand about Bismarck's negative term for the French

parts.note: C, for circa, means about
Otto was the first name of Bismarck, the German chancellor
non is French for no

explanation.surface: A historian starts to grasp Bismarck's dismissive word for the French.
explanation.walkthrough: Bismarck's possessive gives his first name, OTTO, not anything he said.
explanation.definitionFit: To cotton on is an informal idiom for grasping something, starting to understand it.

clue.text: Ending near Milan, odd characters leave the country

indicators.note: the first, third, fifth and every other odd-placed letter departs, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: Near Milan, at the end, strange people quit the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd characters' looks like eccentric people, but means the odd-numbered letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigeria is a country in West Africa.

clue.text: Hate new look of a hotel

indicators.note: giving the words a new look rearranges their letters

explanation.surface: Detesting the hotel's makeover.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe is to detest, a strong synonym for hate.

clue.text: Blue fly settling on deer, you say?

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the words sound like the answer

parts.note: to fly is to soar, and a hart is a deer; soar placed after hart

explanation.surface: A sad tale of an insect landing on a stag, or so you claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' looks like the insect but is the verb soar; 'settling on' puts it after HART, and the whole is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue means sad or downcast, and heartsore is an old word for grieved or sorrowful.

clue.text: Escape not unlawful

explanation.surface: A getaway that was fully within the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Leg it is slang for fleeing, and the same letters as one word are slang for legitimate or lawful.

clue.text: Girl with a fever originating in 20

parts.note: lass is a word for a girl

explanation.surface: A young woman has caught an illness from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: '20' points to 20-down: the fever was first identified there, in the town of Lassa.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassa fever is a viral haemorrhagic fever named after a town in West Africa where it was first recorded.

clue.text: Port passed round by British moneybags

indicators.note: passed round means the port's name is turned to run backwards

parts.note: Oban is a port on the west coast of Scotland

explanation.surface: A wealthy man hands round the port at a British dinner table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the drink handed round after dinner, but it is the town of OBAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Moneybags is a slang term for a rich person, and a nabob is a very wealthy man.

clue.text: Finance expert finally got back, having closed safe

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word got is used
the back closes round, enclosing, the word for safe

parts.note: the rear is the back
sure can mean safe, as in a sure bet

explanation.surface: A financier at last retrieved what was locked in the safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'safe' looks like a strongbox but means certain; 'having closed' has the back word close round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer manages an organisation's money, so is its finance expert.

clue.text: Piece of cake giving you wind?

explanation.surface: Eating a slice of cake gives you indigestion.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeze is informal for an easy task and also a light wind.

clue.text: Labour backed right to get benefit

indicators.note: backed means the abbreviation for right is turned to read the other way

parts.note: avail means benefit, as in 'of no avail'

explanation.surface: The Labour Party supported the right to receive welfare benefits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the British political party but means toil.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is hard toil or painful effort, an old word for labour.
